loader_analysis.fread_approach: stat + fopen + malloc(N*float) + fread(data, float, N) + fclose
loader_analysis.mmap_approach: stat + fopen + fileno + mmap(NULL, N*4, PROT_READ, MAP_PRIVATE, fd, 0) + fclose
loader_analysis.mmap_advantage: avoids malloc(90MB per layer) + fread(90MB per layer); uses OS page cache directly
loader_analysis.fread_sidecar_load_includes: allocation time + copy time + OS I/O (cold or cached)
loader_analysis.mmap_sidecar_load_includes: open/fileno/mmap syscalls only; pages mapped on first access
loader_analysis.validation_scan: no validation scan in either approach — shape detected by file size
loader_analysis.data_resident: both: data stays in memory via g_prt_sidecar_buffers

baseline_fread_cold.description: fread from disk, cold page cache (13AF baseline)

warm_fread.description: fread from disk, warm page cache (back-to-back runs)
warm_fread.note: page cache makes fread faster but still needs malloc+copy

tmpfs.description: fread from tmpfs (/dev/shm), sidecars pre-copied to RAM
tmpfs.memory_pressure: swap usage increased 3.1GB -> 3.8GB during runs; not viable
tmpfs.verdict: BLOCKED_MEMORY - copying 3.1GB to tmpfs first then freading causes page eviction and swap thrash

mmap_disk.description: mmap from disk, warm page cache (OS maps pages directly, no copy)
mmap_disk.note: mmap uses OS page cache — no malloc, no copy, ~0ms load time

derived.mmap_does_not_improve_gen_throughput: gen tok/s unchanged at 8.5-8.6 t/s (kernel is bottleneck)
derived.generation_bottleneck: PRTGEN / native GEN = 0.41x — AVX2 kernel time dominates per-token overhead

optimization_targets_next.priority_1: Per-token kernel overhead (3.3s for 80 tokens = 41ms/call * 272 calls)
optimization_targets_next.priority_2: Graph/dispatch overhead (cb_total == kern_total exactly, so 0% graph overhead)
optimization_targets_next.note: After mmap, sidecar load is no longer the bottleneck. Kernel time dominates.

allowed_claims: mmap reduced sidecar load from 4542ms to 0.14ms (99.97% reduction)
mmap reduced PRT wall time from 9.884s to 5.300s (46.4% reduction)
mmap does not change generation throughput (8.5 vs 8.6 t/s)
After mmap, PRT remains 2.56x slower in wall time vs native (vs fread 4.77x)
mmap is safe and functional: 36/36 sidecars loaded, clean output, 0 fallback
tmpfs is not viable on this 15GB machine due to memory pressure and swap thrash
forbidden_claims: No universal speedup from mmap alone
